subject: Acme: intermittent chunked-transfer drop + websocket heartbeat timeouts
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Support <support@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T22:47:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] Intermittent truncated streaming responses (prod)

Hi Markus,

We started seeing a spike in partial/terminated streaming responses from the Redwood API this evening (around 22:30 PST). The symptom is: the websocket connection remains open but the chunked transfer stops mid-response and the client never receives the final chunk. In other cases the connection returns a 502/504.

Impact: production feature (real-time assistant) is dropping ~8-12% of streaming sessions; traffic ~2k reqs/min to the streaming endpoint. We pulled server logs and included trace IDs in the attached trace_ABC123.json.

Key observations from our side:
- SDK v1.4.0 (Node)
- TCP keepalive set to 30s on our side
- Patterns show chunk truncation after ~10-20s into longer responses

Attaching logs and a screenshot of the console timeout. Can you triage urgently? This is affecting an internal customer demo tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme_error_log_20270314.txt, trace_ABC123.json, screenshot_timeout.png

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-14T23:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Intermittent truncated streaming responses (prod)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear report and the logs. We're on it.

Immediate asks to help our investigation: can you confirm the SDK connection keepalive and retry config (you mentioned 30s), and whether clients are using long-polling fallbacks for any sessions? Also can you share 1-2 raw request IDs from noisy sessions (if not already in trace_ABC123.json)?

Connor and Marissa — looping you in for infra + runtime diagnostics. I will open a PagerDuty incident and aim for a hotfix routing change while we investigate root cause.

Markus
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T07:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: [URGENT] Intermittent truncated streaming responses (prod)

Quick internal notes (initial findings):
- Observed spike in 502/504s at the edge LB matching customer times (logs: NGINX upstream prematurely closed connection).
- Runtime metrics show episodic GPU pool backpressure: token generation latency spikes + queued requests increase for sessions >15s.
- Our chunking layer is timing out on heartbeats when a batch executor switches kernels mid-stream (happens during quantized kernel swapping under load).

Temporary mitigations applied at 07:05: increased websocket keepalive and LB idle timeout to 90s for the affected host pool. Also forced routing for Acme to a larger instance class (r5g-xxlarge-equivalent) to relieve backpressure.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Keep the larger instance routing in place for 2-4 hours while we monitor.
2) Roll back the kernel swapping logic (safe-mode kernel) for the current model family to avoid mid-stream execution path switches.
3) Parallel: collect perf traces for sessions that hit >15s to validate prefix cache thrash hypothesis.

I'll continue to monitor the PagerDuty incident. Marking this high.

—Connor
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Exec FYI: Acme streaming degradation / customer-impacting (prod)

Jordan/Laura — FYI and request for exec support. We have an active high-priority incident affecting Acme Analytics where streaming responses are being truncated (chunked transfer stops mid-response) and websocket clients observe heartbeat timeouts. Customer traffic ~2k rps to the streaming endpoint; error rate has spiked to ~9%.

What we did so far: increased LB timeouts, routed Acme to a larger instance class, and applied a temporary kernel safe-mode to avoid in-flight kernel swaps. Early signal shows error rate falling to ~1.5% after routing change.

Customer asks: 1) urgent fix, 2) confirmation of root cause, 3) compensation for customer impact (they're asking for credits).

Requesting: (a) approval to offer a one-time usage credit if we fail SLA on postmortem findings (b) prioritized support for the Customer Success manager to coordinate the demo tomorrow morning.

Markus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-analytics.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Intermittent truncated streaming responses (prod)

Hi Sarah — quick remediation update:

What we changed at 09:00:
- Permanently pinned Acme sessions to a larger instance class in the affected pool.
- Disabled live kernel swaps for the current model families serving these sessions (applied safe kernel).
- Tuned runtime chunk heartbeat threshold from 8s -> 20s to tolerate transient GC/queueing blips.

Why this likely happened: our kernel selection heuristic can trigger a path change mid-stream when sequence-length stats shift; under high concurrency that can cause temporary KV cache misses and transient execution stalls leading to chunk send timeouts. We're tracking this as a regression caused by a change in the kernel selection rollout last week.

Attachments: trace_ABC123.json (detailed perf trace). We'll run a postmortem and plan a controlled rollback of the rollout that introduced the heuristic.

Next steps:
- Monitoring window 2 hours, then we will start a canary rollback if error rate doesn't remain low.
- Postmortem draft within 48 hours; will include customer impact window and credit calculation if applicable.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is high impact. We will keep you updated every 30 minutes for the next 2 hours.

—Marissa
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
